answer: Harmonic activity decay resists sybils: an identity's influence weight decays unless refreshed by genuine periodic activity, and the refresh cost per identity is constant per period. A dune of dormant fakes fades as the tide of decay runs, so maintaining N sybils at full weight demands N streams of continuous real activity forever, not a one-time spin-up. The vault of accumulated influence leaks steadily; an attacker must keep paying the upkeep on every identity each period, converting a cheap creation burst into a perpetual per-head maintenance bill.
